UPSTREAM: mb/google/hatch: Re-configure GPP_A12 as GPO before entering sleep GPP_A12 has a Native3 (SX_EXIT_HOLDOFF#) mode, which allows to delay resuming to S0. If this pad is not locked and platform was not initially designed for this functionality, malware could reconfigure this pads setting under OS (switch to Native3), which would make platform not able to resume until G3 is applied. To prevent misuse of this pad, re-configure this pad before entering S3 and S5 to guarantee that the pad configuration is correct. CRAS: bt_io - Implement no_stream ops for A2DP/HFP The default no stream function keeps filling zero frames to full device buffer, so when the iodev state changes back to normal stream there is a noticeable delay. This change improves that by adding no_stream ops for A2DP and HFP iodev. By tracking the valid samples to drain, we can adjust the output level to a reasonable value when dev leaves no stream state. BUG=chromium:946356 TEST=Connect BT headset and open YouTube in A2DP and HFP modes. Close and re-open YouTube tab, and grep 'NO_STREAM' in audio thread dump, to verify that the output level is of the stream's callback level at the moment when device leaves no stream state. Change-Id: I3e738b314892527177da3aa0e7f5103076bfd24f Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1536055 Commit-Ready: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Tested-by: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org>

CRAS: HFP - Remove code to dynamically update packet and buffer size Change the main buffer size to 28800 so it's multiple of packet size values we've seen(48, 60, and 128). The old mechanism assumes the SCO packet come in arbitrary size so we have to dynamically change the iodev's buffer_size since it might not divide the main large buffer. The dangerous thing is that the packet size is determined in audio thread, and it may trigger the buffer size change on an iodev when main thread still using it. Thre are only handful of packet size values, it's better we set the main buffer size as their common multiple. BUG=chromium:946356 TEST=Manual test HFP audio Change-Id: Ib7b3fa3411f3526fcfa849eabcc2d2c705491857 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1517343 Commit-Ready: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Tested-by: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Cheng-Yi Chiang <cychiang@chromium.org>

pytest: Don't pickle the python exception. CL:1477132 tried to provide a more structured way to report the raised exception from pytests to goofy. The approach pickles exceptions so that they can be send to the event queue and saved to files. However, most of the exception can't be pickled (see https://bugs.python.org/issue27015 for more detail). This CL revises the related modules to prevent the exception instances from being serialized. `cros.factory.test.test_case.TestCase` now stores the exception instance locally instead of posting it to the event queue directly. `cros.factory.test.pytest_runner` dumps the exception message and its traceback list instead of the whole instance to the output file. BUG=chromium:933275 TEST=make test; manual test Change-Id: I03a6fecf712c01839d2b4bb36d99ca50684ded79 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1545340 Commit-Ready: Yong Hong <yhong@google.com> Tested-by: Yong Hong <yhong@google.com> Reviewed-by: Wei-Han Chen <stimim@chromium.org>

tast: Make test runners send SIGTERM to stale processes. Make test runners enumerate existing process before running tests and send SIGTERM to any processes sharing the same executable. These are likely to be stale processes from earlier (or conflicting) test runs, and they can cause confusing failures if ignored. Also update runners to catch SIGTERM and clean up before exiting to make it less likely that the stale process will leave bundle or test-started processes running.
